title: Act IV, Scene I

teacherSummary.text: Paris tells the Friar of the wedding. Juliet arrives and fences verbally with him. Alone with the Friar, she threatens suicide; he gives her a potion that will make her seem dead for forty-two hours and promises to send for Romeo.

vocabulary.definition: reach; the limit of one's ability
vocabulary.context:

It strains me past the compass of my wits:
I hear thou must, and nothing may prorogue it,
On Thursday next be married to this county.

satQuestions.passage:
Hold, daughter: I do spy a kind of hope,
Which craves as desperate an execution
As that is desperate which we would prevent.
If, rather than to marry County Paris,
Thou hast the strength of will to slay thyself,
Then is it likely thou wilt undertake
A thing like death to chide away this shame,
That copest with death himself to scape from it;
And, if thou darest, I’ll give thee remedy.

symbolsAndMotifs.name: light and dark
symbolsAndMotifs.explanation: The lovers describe each other as light in darkness (torches, sun, stars, lightning), yet they can meet only at night, and daylight brings danger.
